speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: You had a brother on my stair and you did not bring him to the board. I count a mouth that sits.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: He would not stay. The shop wanted him. You have lost nothing that was yours.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then sit. The board is threepence, and the loaf is against the notch.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: It is short again. I laid it with the end to the window.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: A finger and a half. The price is a penny. The penny does not grow because the loaf shrinks. What may this table hear?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The frame in Chapel Street is roofed. The money came safe. She wrote no sum, and I am not going to.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The bailiff's man has not been at my father's porch these two Sundays. My father says it is the weather.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It's the weather. I said it to Gilbert. I am saying it to you. I do not have a better sentence.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: They wrote. The words are upstairs. You may have the roof and the porch. That is the letter, for this house.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then eat. I am not owed a drawing. Gib has been on your book all afternoon.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave him. He lies on the second volume. I will not move him tonight.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: There is beef. It is the end of the piece.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will eat it. Tomorrow the house plays, and I am not in it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then the board will be here. Threepence, the same as today. A letter does not change a loaf.
